scope: Known mathematical framework for fixed uncertain nonnegative edge rates and leaks, matrix interval outer bounds, and general Metzler comparison.
classification: Standard positive/cooperative interval prediction or bounding-system construction. Without output measurements/correction, interval predictor or comparison envelope is more exact terminology than observer.

sources.title: Robust Positive Interval Observers For Uncertain Positive Systems
sources.version: 18th IFAC World Congress preprints, Milano, August 28-September 2, 2011; IFAC Proceedings Volumes 44(1),14330-14334
sources.source_type: Actual IFAC conference preprint hosted in university proceedings archive; publisher metadata independently retrieved.

items: Section4 illustrative mammillary three-compartment flow model Eq16

verified_claims: Metzler means only nonnegative off-diagonal entries. Lemma5 says exp(tM) is nonnegative for every Metzler M; Hurwitz conditions are separate subsequent equivalences.
Remark6 applies positivity to affine forcing via variation of constants; Lemma7 bounds a same-Metzler system from above by replacing bounded forcing with an upper forcing.
Section3 takes elementwise matrix bounds and proves state inclusion by writing error equations with Metzler matrices and nonnegative residual forcing.

Section4 uses compartment flow rates that occur both as positive coupling and negative diagonal contributions, then constructs separate matrix entry bounds. This is closely aligned with the project's parameter splitting.
sources.boundary: For observer optimization and asymptotic error bounds, the paper imposes extra boundedness/stability hypotheses. Those are not needed for the basic finite-time containment mechanism and should not be silently borrowed as automatic.

sources.source_type: Author preprint and author project page

items: direct interval predictor instability despite stable original dynamics

verified_claims: Entrywise matrix uncertainty and sign-split interval arithmetic give a standard direct interval predictor with guaranteed state containment.
Introduction and SectionIII.B explicitly separate containment from stability: interval outer inclusion can transform stable dynamics into an unstable predictor.
Theorem1 proves containment first and establishes input-to-state stability only under additional matrix inequalities. Hence an expanding outer bound is not by itself a failed containment proof.
sources.boundary: The paper's proposed tighter LPV predictor is not identical to the project's simpler entrywise envelope. Its relevance is the general interval arithmetic/Metzler framework and the explicit stability caveat.

sources.title: Monotone Control Systems
sources.source_type: Author-hosted published paper plus author preprint; read in prior phase of same subagent task
sources.verified_claim: State cooperativity concerns off-diagonal derivatives; monotonicity with respect to another input or parameter additionally requires the corresponding parameter derivatives to have the chosen fixed signs. Nonnegative physical parameters alone do not establish parameter monotonicity.

assumptions: appropriate continuous/absolutely-continuous solution and derivative equation
project_comparison.comparison_proof: Let y'=Mbar y+fhi with y(0)>=x(0). Error e=y-x obeys e'=Mbar e+r. Off-diagonal entries of Mbar are nonnegative, so exp(Mbar t)>=0 even if a diagonal entry is positive; therefore e>=0.
project_comparison.conservation_boundary: Mbar generally need not be any physically admissible parameter realization, conservative, stochastic, dissipative or Hurwitz. State containment follows from cooperativity and the residual sign.
project_comparison.parameter_dependency: Each edge rate affects both positive inflow and negative loss. Treating those two occurrences independently loses algebraic dependency and may widen the box; that widening is allowed for an outer certificate.
project_comparison.self_edge_refinement: If self edges are allowed, actual a_ii terms cancel exactly. Cancelling self terms before interval enclosure gives the tighter diagonal -sum_{j!=i}alo_ij-dlo_i. The stated coarse bound remains valid but can introduce an artificial positive diagonal through ahi_ii-alo_ii.
project_comparison.regularity_boundary: The same algebra does not require rates to be fixed: it also works for time-varying rates staying within the bounds, provided the differential relation and solution regularity hold. This wider fact is standard, not asserted as implemented by the project.
project_comparison.terminology: With no measured-output correction, call the construction an interval predictor, upper comparison system, or robust outer envelope.

counterexample.status: Original elementary example derived here to explain a standard limitation; not claimed as a literature example or research novelty.
counterexample.model: x0'=-k x0, x1'=k x0-x1, x(0)=(1,0), fixed k in [2,6], input zero.
counterexample.matrix: M(k)=[[-k,0],[k,-1]], Metzler and Hurwitz for every k in [2,6].
counterexample.reason: The parameter k appears with opposite signs in the two equations: partial f/partial k=(-x0,+x0). Thus ordinary coordinate order does not make this a monotone parameter input, despite positive state dynamics.
counterexample.matrix_box: The sharp entrywise upper matrix across this family is [[-2,0],[6,-1]], obtained by selecting a lower k for the negative diagonal and an upper k for the positive coupling. It is not M(k) for any single k; this is precisely a legitimate interval outer relaxation.
